idiom_name: plain object with a type field + handler lookup table
implementation_notes: JavaScript already treats data as dynamic objects and JSON as its native interchange format, so the command class hierarchy collapses into a tagged object literal ({ type, payload }) and dispatch becomes a handler map or a switch on type - the simpler local idiom replaces the classic structure. Delivery is whatever channel is at hand: structured-clone postMessage to a worker thread, or JSON over a broker client such as amqplib, BullMQ or a WebSocket, which is where the library-shaped part of the pattern lives. Classes are justified only when a command carries behavior locally (undo stacks, macro recording).
pitfalls: A bare object is not a contract: a typo in the type string only fails at dispatch time, so validate the tag and payload at the channel boundary.
JSON.stringify drops undefined values, functions and prototypes and converts Date to a string, so a payload that works in memory may not survive the wire.
postMessage uses the structured clone algorithm, which cannot clone class instances with prototypes or functions - a command sent as an instance arrives as a plain object and its methods are gone.
